entities.summary:
Martin Agricola was a German composer of Renaissance music and a music theorist.

Born in the late 15th century, Agricola was a key figure in the development of polyphonic music in Germany.

His most famous work, the 'De inventione musicorum' ('The Discovery of Music'), was published in 1500 and became a seminal text in the field of music theory.

Agricola's compositions, which often featured complex polyphonic textures, were widely performed during his lifetime and have since been rediscovered and celebrated by musicologists.

Agricola's legacy can be seen in the works of later composers, such as Hans Weissenbach and Nikolaus Kern.

One of Agricola's most notable compositions is his 'Missa in honorem Sancti Michaelis', a complex and beautiful mass setting that showcases his mastery of polyphonic music.

Agricola's contributions to music theory and composition have had a lasting impact on the development of Western classical music.

In 2015, the German city of Lübeck dedicated a monument to Agricola, recognizing his significance as a composer and music theorist.

Agricola's work continues to inspire and influence composers and musicologists to this day.

The 'Missa in honorem Sancti Michaelis' has been recorded by several ensembles and is considered a highlight of Agricola's oeuvre.

Agricola's influence can also be seen in the works of later composers, such as Bach and Mozart, who were influenced by his compositions and music theory.

In 2010, the University of Lübeck published a critical edition of Agricola's 'De inventione musicorum', which has become a standard reference work in the field of musicology.
